clue.text: Leading man that has two parts on stage

definitions.text: Leading man that has two parts on stage

parts.words: Leading man that has two parts on stage
parts.note: Shakespeare wrote two history plays, Part 1 and Part 2, about this king, so the title role is a leading man with two parts

explanation.surface: An actor boasts of a lead role in which he plays two characters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two parts' reads as a double role, but it is the two plays: Henry IV Part 1 and Henry IV Part 2.
explanation.definitionFit: The English king Henry IV is the title figure of both Shakespeare plays bearing his name.

clue.text: Bewitched, in part, using new spell

indicators.note: spelling a word anew means writing its letters in a fresh order, so the word part is rearranged

explanation.surface: A sorcerer's victim, partly enchanted by a freshly cast spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spell' pretends to be magic, fitting 'Bewitched', but here it means to spell out letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone rapt is utterly entranced, as if held under an enchantment.

clue.text: Brutal, apart from having silver lining

indicators.note: having something as a lining means holding it within, so one piece goes inside the other
a lining sits on the inside, so the silver goes within the other word

parts.note: save, as in 'all save one', means apart from
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A cruel act, redeemed only by its silver lining.
explanation.definitionFit: Savage and brutal are synonyms for fierce, violent cruelty.

clue.text: Almost back, holding it up as part of the Guardian, say

indicators.note: holding means one piece contains the other inside it
almost means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to back a motion is to second it

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word it is read from bottom to top, so backwards

explanation.surface: A newspaper reader nearly turning back, holding a page of the Guardian up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims SECOND to SECON; 'up' turns IT into TI, which SECON is 'holding'.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper is divided into sections, such as sport or business, so the Guardian is an example.

clue.text: List of parts a repairman tossed out

indicators.note: out means the letters are thrown into disorder, so these words are rearranged together

explanation.surface: A mechanic's parts list, thrown away by a repairman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tossed out' looks like one phrase, but 'tossed' is part of the fodder: A REPAIRMAN plus TOSSED, with 'out' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The dramatis personae is the cast list printed at the start of a play, naming its roles.

clue.text: Direction to players to reduce noise — part of one I composed

definitions.text: Direction to players to reduce noise

indicators.note: composed means put together anew, so these letters are arranged into another order

explanation.surface: A composer's score tells the players to quieten down in one passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' sounds like actors, but these are musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian musical marking means loud then immediately soft, telling musicians to drop the volume.

clue.text: Partly withdraw, making borders of state change and decrease

indicators.note: making signals that the word is made to take on a new letter
change says one letter of the word is swapped for another

parts.note: to recede is to diminish or decrease

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its outer letters; here the opening one

explanation.surface: A state partly pulls back, changing its borders and shrinking.
explanation.walkthrough: RECEDE's borders are R and E; changing them to those of STATE (S and E) swaps only the R for S.
explanation.definitionFit: To secede is for one part of a nation or union to formally withdraw from it.

clue.text: Part — with ease, if broken?

indicators.note: broken means the letters are smashed and reassembled in another order

explanation.surface: Parting is easy once things have broken down.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: PART with EASE, broken up, gives a word meaning 'part'.
explanation.definitionFit: To separate is to part, divide or move away from one another.

clue.text: Part of greater honesty that's starting to be seen between Swiss banks

definitions.text: that's starting to be seen between Swiss banks

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Swiss bankers are slowly being seen as more honest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swiss banks' suggests finance, but these are riverbanks: the Rhône rises in Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhône river rises in a Swiss glacier and flows between banks in Switzerland before entering France.

clue.text: Idiot getting role after change of heart

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, and changing it here shifts a central letter to a new place

parts.note: an actor's part is their role

explanation.surface: A fool lands an acting role after changing his mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Prat is British slang for a stupid or foolish person.

clue.text: Part of pageant I'm at — terrific ephemeral stuff

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A spectator says the pageant they are at is terrific, but fleeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Antimatter is short-lived: it annihilates on meeting ordinary matter, so it is fleeting material.

clue.text: Small part of statistical report for firm

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a table of figures is a typical component of a statistical report

explanation.surface: A statistician files a small section of a report for a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like a company, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Stable and firm both mean steady and not likely to move or give way.

clue.text: Unfathomable part in Shakespearean comedy? Not so

parts.note: Bottom is the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream
less means not so much, as in 'less bright' for 'not so bright'

explanation.surface: A puzzled theatregoer finds a role in a Shakespeare comedy baffling, then thinks again.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bottomless has no floor to reach, so its depth cannot be sounded or fathomed.

clue.text: Part of big issue to be raised in old court — increased rent

parts.note: up means raised or increased, as in prices being up
to let is to rent out

explanation.surface: A tenant takes an old-fashioned court case over a rent increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' means offspring, so a 'big issue' is a large litter, and an octuplet is one of eight born at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a formal word for children; an octuplet is one of eight siblings from a single birth.

clue.text: Formalities progressively reduced, with two parts switched

indicators.note: the word splits into two chunks that swap places, the end chunk going to the front

parts.note: something tapered narrows gradually towards one end

explanation.surface: Bureaucratic procedures were cut down step by step, with two sections exchanged.
explanation.walkthrough: TAPERED splits as TAPE and RED; switching them gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Red tape is excessive official procedure, the formalities of bureaucracy.

clue.text: See 5
Quarter thus includes area for grass

parts.note: E, east, is one of the four quarters or compass points

indicators.note: includes means one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
a part of a town or country is an area

explanation.surface: A district that thereby takes in an area for lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Esparto is a tough Spanish grass used for making rope and paper.

clue.text: Hear test broadcast in places where many a player takes part

definitions.text: places where many a player takes part

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into another order

explanation.surface: A sound test is aired at venues where actors perform.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatres are venues where actors, or players, take roles in performances.

clue.text: Bit by bit, go inside controlling mechanism in parts of country

indicators.note: inside means the letters are placed within the other word
by sets the first bit beside and into the controlling mechanism, one letter at a time

parts.note: reins are the straps a rider uses to control a horse

indicators.note: the first bit of the word go is taken on its own, one letter as a single bit

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the second bit of the word go is its closing letter, taken separately from the first

explanation.surface: Gradually a part slides into its control mechanism in country areas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit by bit' sounds like gradually, or a horse's bit, but it says the two letters of 'go' enter the reins separately rather than as one block.
explanation.definitionFit: Regions are areas or districts into which a country is divided.

clue.text: Starters for our first part of meal, naturally

indicators.note: starters are the opening items, so the first letters of the following words are taken

parts.note: a course is one stage of a meal, such as the starter or main

explanation.surface: Choosing the starters for the first part of our meal, as you would expect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starters' suggests food, fitting the meal, but it picks first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Of course' and 'naturally' are both phrases of ready agreement meaning obviously.

clue.text: See 1
Engine parts — throttles

definitions.meaning: valves in a carburettor controlling air intake

explanation.surface: A mechanic on engine components that regulate fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: A choke restricts air to an engine; to choke someone is to strangle them by the throat.

clue.text: About to depart or part forcefully

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
to leave is to depart

explanation.surface: Someone choosing between leaving now or splitting with force.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleave is to split something apart with a heavy blow, as an axe does.

clue.text: Bunch elected in cunning way to expedite part of bill

definitions.text: way to expedite part of bill

indicators.note: in signals that the first pieces are placed inside the word that follows

parts.note: guile is cunning or craftiness
a lot is a bunch or group
a candidate who is elected is in

explanation.surface: A clique of elected members devise a sly way to rush a bill.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK Parliament a guillotine is a timetable motion that cuts short debate on stages of a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliamentary guillotine sets fixed time limits so parts of a bill are passed without further debate.

clue.text: Final parts in cast recast for theatrical hit

indicators.note: the final parts are the last two letters, which alone are turned round
recast says the letters are cast again in a fresh order, here the closing pair flipped

explanation.surface: A show recast in its final stages becomes a big hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Cats is Andrew Lloyd Webber's long-running musical, a huge stage success.

clue.text: You may part with this part of fowl

definitions.meaning: the red crest on a chicken's head

explanation.definitionFit: A comb divides hair into a parting; the fleshy crest on a cockerel's head is also called a comb.

clue.text: Part for Maria Callas to study endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to scan is to study closely

explanation.surface: A soprano must keep studying a role without end.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosca, the title role in Puccini's opera, was one of the great soprano Maria Callas's signature roles.

clue.text: Nothing remaining from fire around very cold part of year

indicators.note: around means these pieces enclose the next one

parts.note: no means none, nothing
an ember is a glowing piece left after a fire

explanation.surface: No embers left in the grate in a bitterly cold season.
explanation.definitionFit: November is a late-autumn month, chilly in the northern hemisphere.
